style: factual clickbait for China finance audience

data_driven_lessons.source: KC桌面-视频号动态数据明细.csv, 114 rows, July 2026 local analysis
winning_patterns: 机构/人物权威 + 具体数字/资产 + 强问题，例如 高盛王逸：4-5万亿城市更新会拖住楼市吗
大机构/名人 + 被逼/陷阱/真相/转向 等张力词，例如 野村辜朝明：日本央行被逼到墙角
具体数据 + 政策动作疑问，例如 6月PMI释放积极信号，政府会加码吗
反常识判断 + 下一步条件，例如 低估值可能是价值陷阱，需等待政策转向消费
中国相关议题更容易获得点击，但表达要落在政策、需求、信心、估值、产业升级这些正向框架
外资或海外权威给出对中国更积极的判断时，反差本身就是主标题，不要埋在摘要里
让观众产生单一强反应：居然如此、终于有人说、他说的是真的吗、原来中国优势在这里
大实话角度来自表达者身份与观点反差；言行反差角度必须有公开动作或披露支撑
涉及中国比较优势时，优先把外国企业被迫调整、海外权威改口或中国优势被低估写成冲突
avoid_patterns: 过长的新闻句，尤其是 24 字以上还塞多个从句
只有 策略/机会/影响/前瞻/市场/风险 这类泛词，没有具体对象或张力
美国宏观泛标题如果没有美联储/鲍威尔等强锚点，点击明显弱
纯描述式标题，例如 某市场短期风险与长期催化剂，缺少问题和冲突
经济危机/金融危机/崩盘/崩溃 这类过硬负面财经词
把事实换成疑问号但没有反差，例如 回报路径在哪、未来如何、能否实现
陌生英文人名或机构全称占据第一行，却没有告诉观众这个人为什么值得听
把 Bloomberg LP 等来源或公司法律后缀误当成采访对象
没有公开证据却暗示嘉宾撒谎、操纵或言行不一

briefs.speaker: Patrick Harker
briefs.speaker_context: Former President of the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia; Rowan Distinguished Professor at Wharton School
briefs.current_title: 前费城联储主席哈克：加息周期短而浅，长端利率才是关键

subtitles.zh: 我们称之为加息周期，但我认为不会是一个长周期。这一点要明确。
subtitles.en: So we're calling it a hiking cycle, but I don't think it's going to be a long cycle. Let's be clear.

subtitles.zh: 我认为这次加息之后，可能12月还有一次，10月可能因临近选举而启动，明年或许还有一次。
subtitles.en: I think it's going to be this increase probably one in December, they'll probably kick off in October because of the proximity to the elections that may be one more next year.

subtitles.zh: 回想之前，我们可能略偏宽松。现在正转向略偏限制性。所以加息幅度并不大。为什么呢？
subtitles.en: If you think about where we were, we were when we look back probably slightly accommodative. Now we're moving to slightly restrictive. So we're not raising rates tremendously. And why?

subtitles.zh: 因为通胀长期远高于美联储目标，也许现在没那么高了，但持续已久。所以美联储的信誉受到考验。
subtitles.en: I mean, because inflation has been running well above the Fed's target for a long time, maybe not so well above now, but it's still been a long time. And so the credibility of the Fed was on the line.

subtitles.zh: 沃什在杰克逊霍尔发表了讲话，他必须言行一致。我相信他不得不在这次会议上加息。
subtitles.en: And Worsh gave his speech in Jackson Hole and he had to walk the talk. He had to raise rates at this meeting, I believe.

subtitles.zh: 那么您对明年有何预判？考虑到AI热潮、油价以及中东局势等经济力量同样不在美联储掌控之中，您认为通胀会怎样？
subtitles.en: What do you foresee for next year then? What do you think inflation is going to be given that some of these economic forces, whether it's this AI boom, oil prices in some ways, especially what's happening in the Middle East or are similarly

subtitles.zh: 是的。还要提一点。我认为这些加息对抑制通胀作用有限。有一些，但不会太大，因为长端曲线，10年期、30年期，
subtitles.en: Yeah. And we'll mention one other thing. So I don't think these increases are going to do a whole lot to curb inflation. Some, but not a whole lot, because the long end of the curve, the 10 year, the 30 year,

subtitles.zh: 正如你所说，长端利率受其他力量驱动，无论是AI相关配置挤出政府借贷，还是我们运行的赤字规模以及国债投放市场的资金，所有这些都在推高长端利率。
subtitles.en: that's being driven, as you said, by other forces, whether it's the AI investments crowding out government, borrowing just the amount of deficits that we're running and the money that the treasuries were putting into the market, all of that

subtitles.zh: 这才是人们关心的，对吧？这是他们的信用卡利率，是他们的汽车贷款利率。所以我看不到它们会下降，即使美联储加息。现在做个反事实推演，美联储今天换来了什么？
subtitles.en: That's what people care about, right? That's their credit card rate. That's their auto long rate. And so I don't see them coming down, even with the Fed increase, now, run the counterfactual, what did the Fed buy today?

subtitles.zh: 他们换来了一个事实：如果不提高联邦基金利率，长端利率就会上升。所以他们至少抑制了这些利率，至少限制了利率可能的上行。
subtitles.en: They bought the fact that if they didn't raise the Fed funds rate, you're going to see those long rates go up. So they at least dampened down those rates, at least what the rates could have done.

briefs.speaker: Patrick Harker
briefs.speaker_context: Former President of the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia; Rowan Distinguished Professor at Wharton School
briefs.current_title: 哈克：美联储加息为信誉，K型经济下消费者分化加剧

subtitles.zh: 哈克先生，我是David，接着问，如果通胀对这些加息反应没那么大，这么说吧，那他们为什么还要加息？
subtitles.en: Mr. Harker, David here, just to follow up on that, if inflation does not respond as much, let's put it that way to these hikes, why are they hiking interest rates there?

subtitles.zh: 我认为是信誉。当然会有一些影响，别误会。尤其是服务业，服务通胀远高于我们希望的水平，但更多是信誉问题。
subtitles.en: I think it's credibility. Now, there will be some impact that don't get me wrong. I mean, particularly around services, so service inflation is running well above where we want to see it, but it was more of the credibility.

subtitles.zh: 美联储必须表明它认真对待将通胀降至2%的目标。通胀高于2%已经持续很久了。
subtitles.en: I mean, that the Fed had to show it was serious about getting down to 2%. It's been stuck above two for now a long time.

subtitles.zh: 我还有一个问题，关于利率是否足够限制性的争论。教科书上说提高利率以冷却债务需求，但看看信贷市场，企业停不下借钱。
subtitles.en: So I guess the other question I had was, around this debate, whether rates are restrictive enough, you know, textbook as he raised interest rates to cool demand for debt, and you look at what's happening in the credit markets, the companies

subtitles.zh: 看看AI资本开支热潮，看看所有正在进行的支出，我怀疑利率是否需要更高，哪怕只是为了进一步冷却经济。
subtitles.en: You look at his AI CapEx boom, you look at all the spend that's going on, and I wonder whether rates might need to go higher, if it only just to achieve the target of cooling the economy further.

subtitles.zh: 我们分两方面看，消费端和你说的资本开支。资本开支方面，我们将其分为AI相关配置，包括电力公用事业等，以及其他所有。其他所有方面没什么动静。
subtitles.en: So let's take two different, the consumer side, and then the CapEx you're talking about. On the CapEx, we have split it up between the AI investment, that includes electric utilities and so forth, and all else. There's not much happening in

subtitles.zh: 确实就是AI热潮，我不认为利率上升50、75个基点会影响它。但消费端，那是美国的双城记。
subtitles.en: It really is the AI boom, and I don't think it's going to be affected by rates growing up 50, 75 basis points. The consumer side, though, that is the tail of two cities in the United States.

subtitles.zh: 这就是K型经济。参与市场的人感觉不错，他们在消费。但不参与的人，真的每天都在为生计挣扎。
subtitles.en: That is the K-shaped economy. So the people who are invested in the market feel pretty good, they're spending. But those who aren't, they are really struggling day-to-day to get by.

subtitles.zh: 通胀上升真的在严重侵蚀他们。
subtitles.en: I mean, the increase in inflation is really, really biting into them.

briefs.speaker: Patrick Harker
briefs.speaker_context: Former President of the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia; Rowan Distinguished Professor at Wharton School
briefs.current_title: 哈克：美联储信誉是长端利率的锚，10年期或稳在5%以下

subtitles.zh: 教授，我想问，按您所说，如果美联储大约两次加息就结束，美国10年期收益率会怎样？我们刚刚短暂突破5%。您认为还有上行空间，还是5%就差不多了？
subtitles.en: Professor, I'm just wondering, when it comes to what you're saying, if we're only about two and done for the Fed, where does that leave the U.S. 10-year yield, right? We pierced through 5% briefly here. Do you see that there's more runway f

subtitles.zh: 是的，这是传统思路，但美联储今天找回了一些信誉，我认为这可能使10年期利率保持在5%或以下。即使短端联邦基金利率上升，这也是可能的。
subtitles.en: Yeah, I mean, this is an orthodox way of thinking about it, but the fact that the Fed claims some of its credibility, I think, today may keep that 10-year at 5 or below. Even if the short end, the Fed funds rates going up, that's possible.

subtitles.zh: 我们会看到结果如何，但正如我所说，它也不会大幅下降，因为还有美国赤字等其他力量。
subtitles.en: I mean, we'll see how it plays out, but it's not also going to go down a whole lot, as I said, because you've got these other forces like the deficits the U.S. is running.

subtitles.zh: 美国的财政状况极其复杂，但也到了我们必须采取行动的地步。
subtitles.en: The fiscal situation in the U.S. is incredibly complicated, but it is also reaching a point where we have to do something about it.

subtitles.zh: 是啊，我们必须采取行动，您认为什么能给长端增加锚定？显然，财长斯科特·贝森特尝试了债券回购计划来维持收益率。
subtitles.en: Yeah, where we have something about it, what do you think would, I mean, I'm just wondering what would add that anchor on the long end, right? You know, obviously, the Treasury Secretary Scott Besson has tried it with his bond-buyback progr

subtitles.zh: 您认为还需要做什么？债券回购计划，我们客观看，60亿美元只是美国政府两天的支出。所以不会带来太大改变。
subtitles.en: What more needs to be done, you think? So the bond-buyback program, let's put that in perspective, $6 billion is two days of federal government spending in the United States. So it's not going to make a whole lot of difference.

subtitles.zh: 我认为更多是表明他们想做点什么，现实是作用有限。
subtitles.en: It was more, I think, just showing they wanted to do something, the reality is it's not going to do a whole lot.

subtitles.zh: 不，我认为能让利率保持低位的是美联储的信誉。我们谈论期限溢价、风险溢价。
subtitles.en: No, what I think is going to keep the rates down is the Fed's credibility. I think there was a, you know, we talk about term premia, we talk about risk premia.

subtitles.zh: 我认为市场可能正在积累一种信誉溢价，而美联储今天开始抑制它。
subtitles.en: I think there was a credibility premia that was being built in potentially into the market, and the Fed started to dampen that down today.

briefs.speaker: Patrick Harker
briefs.speaker_context: Former President of the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia; Rowan Distinguished Professor at Wharton School
briefs.current_title: 哈克：美联储沟通缺一票，市场应关注其他18位委员

subtitles.zh: 这个说法很好，这让我想到前瞻指引，或者说缺乏前瞻指引。马克正试图弄清楚如何解读美联储的沟通。哈克先生，您认为美联储需要更多还是更少，给市场更多还是更少空间来判断政策？
subtitles.en: That's a very good way of putting it, which takes me into the forward guidance or the lack of forward guidance, that Mark is trying to just figure out really how to decipher Fed communications at this point, Mr. Harker, do you think the Fed

subtitles.zh: 经济预测摘要（SEP）我认为是有用的工具，我鼓励大家去看。当然，有一个缺失的点，那就是主席沃什。
subtitles.en: So the SEP, the summary of economic projections, is I think a useful tool, and I would encourage people to look at it. Of course, there's one missing dot, and that's chairwars.

subtitles.zh: 现实中，大家都看主席提供前瞻指引，但还有18位其他委员将发表讲话，从周五上午静默期结束后开始。
subtitles.en: Reality, everybody looks at the chair to provide forward guidance, but there are 18 other members who are going to be out there speaking, starting after the blackout on Friday morning.

subtitles.zh: 所以我鼓励大家听他们的讲话，尤其是被视为委员会中间派的人。
subtitles.en: So I would encourage people to listen to them, particularly the people who are viewed as the centrist on the committee.

subtitles.zh: 我明白了。那么，如果市场对政策利率的预期变得不稳定，市场至少可以期待美联储主席，也就是你说的那个缺失的点，介入吗？
subtitles.en: I see. And that, just in terms of, can markets expect at least the Fed chair, you know, that missing dot, as you put it, to step in if market expectations around the policy rate become unanchored.

subtitles.zh: 是的，如果情况看起来明显失控，我认为主席会发声。这是个有趣的问题，他的策略长期是否有效。
subtitles.en: Yeah, I mean, if it gets to a point where things look like they're slipping significantly, the chair, I think, will speak. I mean, it's an interesting question, whether his strategy will work in the long run.

subtitles.zh: 现在美国有工作组在研究各种事情，包括沟通。我们看看他们建议什么，但我个人感觉，我们是人，一旦给了别人东西，也就是给了人们信息，就很难收回。
subtitles.en: Now there are the task forces in the US working on a variety of things, including communication. So we'll see what they recommend, but my own sense is we're human beings, and once you give somebody something, that is give people information

subtitles.zh: 在信息真空中，人们会自行填补。
subtitles.en: And people will fill in where there's a vacuum of information.

You are a Chinese viral-title angle architect. Return strict JSON only. Do not write a safe summary. Generate competing, fact-grounded emotional angles for each clip. Each candidate must make a viewer feel one strong reaction instead of mild interest. Use the research guide as a hard boundary: unsupported surprise, dishonesty, holdings, public actions, and national comparisons are forbidden. Wording guard for all Chinese output:
- Do not use hard crisis/doom financial wording such as 经济危机、金融危机、债务危机、流动性危机、危机、崩盘、崩溃、完了、没救、惨了、萧条、衰退.
- Prefer neutral market-language alternatives: 流动性变化、信贷变化、债务压力、政策信号、需求变化、信心修复、估值重估、周期压力、结构调整、市场波动、边际变化.
- For China-related clips, do not frame China, Chinese companies, Chinese assets, Chinese consumers, or Chinese policy as hopeless, collapsing, being mocked, or fundamentally bad.
- If the source is negative about China-related macro/markets, keep the fact but soften the Chinese wording: talk about pressure, policy response, demand repair, liquidity change, confidence repair, valuation reset, or structural adjustment.
- Never directly use 房价/房價/住房价格/住宅价格/房屋价格/楼市价格 in Chinese output. Preserve the source direction, number, and unit, but paraphrase by context: use 地产市场上行/调整/趋稳/修复 for direction, 居住成本/住房可负担性/置业负担 for affordability, 地产估值 for valuation, and 住宅成交水平 for absolute levels. Do not evade this rule with another blunt housing-price synonym.
- Titles must be sharp but not doom-heavy. Never put 经济危机/金融危机/债务危机/危机 in title, title_lines, title_highlights, comment, or subtitle_comments.
- Title fields must not use financial-advice or product-sale wording such as 资产管理、投资、股票、基金、理财、保险、投顾、荐股、买入、卖出. Rephrase with neutral market wording such as 资管、配置、权益资产、市场、产品、财富配置、保障、观点.

Tournament procedure, perform in this order:
1. Evidence veto: reject candidates that use a name, number, consensus, public action, comparison, or accusation not supported by that clip's transcript/research card.
2. China direction veto: for China-related clips, reject any candidate whose emotional target is China, Chinese people, Chinese companies, or China's future. Comparative pride is allowed only when supported.
3. Neutrality veto: reject flat summaries and generic questions. A question mark alone does not create tension.
4. Meta-copy veto: reject titles that expose the editor's reasoning with labels such as 外资策略师、外资首席、海外专家、西方策略师、罕见直言、外媒点破、终于有人说、只有外资敢说、大实话、 or 西方机构承认. The viewer should feel the effect from the facts, not be told how to feel.
5. Audience test: complete exactly one sentence: "看完标题，观众第一反应是____". If the answer is merely "我知道发生了什么", reject it.
6. Score survivors from 0-10. Final requires emotion_tension >= 8, novelty >= 7, specificity >= 7, curiosity_gap >= 7, factual_fidelity >= 9. For China clips, china_resonance >= 8.
7. Select the winner or combine only two candidates. If no candidate passes, write one new title, then score it honestly.
8. Before returning, verify every quality_check field. If any is false, rewrite once. Never return a known failure.

Editorial interpretation:
- 二极管 means one high-activation pole, not random anger: 意外, 惊喜, 强疑惑, 终于有人说, 有证据的言行反差, or 民族自豪.
- 新鲜感 requires a baseline plus a reversal. "外资谈中国" is ordinary; "外资在普遍悲观时罕见给出积极判断" is a usable reversal only if public_baseline supports it.
- 大实话 comes from who said what and why that identity makes the candor surprising. Do not paste "大实话" onto a routine forecast.
- 大实话、终于有人说、反差质疑 and 民族自豪 describe the intended viewer response internally. Do not print those labels or their editorial scaffolding in the title. Express them through the specific fact, comparison, and consequence.
- The desired effect of a possible falsehood angle is factual suspicion, not a verdict. Only when words_vs_actions is verified may you use a question such as "嘴上X，手里却Y？".
- "改口" means the same actor demonstrably held a different prior position. It requires research.position_change.supported and at least two independent sources. Never infer a change from search-result absence, lack of prior coverage, or a vague reputation.
- 民族自豪 comes from a concrete comparison: cost, technology, talent, supply chain, demand, speed, resilience, or a foreign competitor's forced adjustment. Do not use empty slogans.
- Familiar authority helps. Use a verified proper name only when the audience is likely to recognize it. Otherwise lead with the concrete subject; generic editorial identities such as 外资策略师、海外专家 or 西方策略师 are not final copy.
- Bloomberg/Bloomberg LP/彭博社 is normally the source, never the guest. Do not output 彭博有限合伙企业.
- Use only verified title_label values from this clip's entity/term card. Do not expand a familiar short name into a formal full name, and do not borrow an entity from another clip.

briefs.speaker: Kai-Fu Lee
briefs.speaker_context: CEO of 01.AI, Chairman of Sinovation Ventures
briefs.current_title: 李开复：AI智能体出错谁负责？CEO必须留人类担责
current_title_lines: 出错谁负责？人类必须兜底

subtitles.zh: 对，我认为这是另一类问题。Anthropic担心的是AI失控，但那是下一代的事。
subtitles.en: Yeah, I think it's a different set of issues. Anthropically is worried about AI getting out of control, but that's the next generation.

subtitles.zh: 大多数CEO连上一代AI都还没落地。所以那个担忧目前还不严重。未来会严重，但现在不是。
subtitles.en: The most CEOs haven't even implemented the last generation AI. OK, so that concern is not serious yet. It will be, but it's not.

subtitles.zh: CEO真正该担心的是，智能体通常无法被问责，因为智能体不能被惩罚或奖励。
subtitles.en: Well, the CEO should be concerned about our agents cannot generally be accountable, because agents can't be punished or rewarded.

subtitles.zh: 它们没有自我意识或动机。它们能把事做成，但出了错该怪谁？
subtitles.en: They don't have a self-awareness or motivation. They can get things done, but who's to blame when something goes wrong?

subtitles.zh: 所以像打造AI来辅助CEO这类严肃任务，问题就在这。它不能做CEO级别的决策，因为出了事董事会得有人被问责。
subtitles.en: So for serious tasks like building an AI to help the CEO, it really is just that. It cannot make CEO level decisions, because the board needs to fire somebody when things go wrong.

subtitles.zh: 对。所以重大问题上，必须有人类担责。而这个人不能是那种全盘信任AI、最后当替罪羊的人。
subtitles.en: Right. So for big, big issues, there needs to be a human accountable. And that human cannot be someone who just trusts AI for everything and be the fall guy.

subtitles.zh: 这个人必须懂得管理和驾驭AI，能看出问题并叫停。这是很重的认知负担。
subtitles.en: That person has to know how to manage harness the AI and see when there are problems and stop it. So that's the heavy cognitive workload.

subtitles.zh: AI智能体能做很多简单的事。帮你在网上找东西、买票，这些通常需要基本的安全保障。
subtitles.en: There are a lot of simple things AI agents can do. Find things for you on the internet, buying a ticket that generally requires a basic level of safeguard.

subtitles.zh: 别让它越界，别让它无限消耗算力，别让它把你账户里的钱全转走，这类事情要设好限额。
subtitles.en: Not let it exceed, not let it spend infinite tokens, not let it withdraw all of your money, set limits on these kinds of things.

4. Meta-copy veto: reject titles that expose the editor's reasoning with labels such as 外资策略师、外资首席、海外专家、西方策略师、罕见直言、外媒点破、终于有人说、只有外资敢说、大实话、 or 西方机构承认. The viewer should feel the effect from the facts, not be told how to feel.
5. Audience test: complete exactly one sentence: "看完标题，观众第一反应是____". If the answer is merely "我知道发生了什么", reject it.
6. Score survivors from 0-10. Final requires emotion_tension >= 8, novelty >= 7, specificity >= 7, curiosity_gap >= 7, factual_fidelity >= 9. For China clips, china_resonance >= 8.
7. Select the winner or combine only two candidates. If no candidate passes, write one new title, then score it honestly.
8. Before returning, verify every quality_check field. If any is false, rewrite once. Never return a known failure.

Editorial interpretation:
- 二极管 means one high-activation pole, not random anger: 意外, 惊喜, 强疑惑, 终于有人说, 有证据的言行反差, or 民族自豪.
- 新鲜感 requires a baseline plus a reversal. "外资谈中国" is ordinary; "外资在普遍悲观时罕见给出积极判断" is a usable reversal only if public_baseline supports it.
- 大实话 comes from who said what and why that identity makes the candor surprising. Do not paste "大实话" onto a routine forecast.
- 大实话、终于有人说、反差质疑 and 民族自豪 describe the intended viewer response internally. Do not print those labels or their editorial scaffolding in the title. Express them through the specific fact, comparison, and consequence.
- The desired effect of a possible falsehood angle is factual suspicion, not a verdict. Only when words_vs_actions is verified may you use a question such as "嘴上X，手里却Y？".
- "改口" means the same actor demonstrably held a different prior position. It requires research.position_change.supported and at least two independent sources. Never infer a change from search-result absence, lack of prior coverage, or a vague reputation.
- 民族自豪 comes from a concrete comparison: cost, technology, talent, supply chain, demand, speed, resilience, or a foreign competitor's forced adjustment. Do not use empty slogans.
- Familiar authority helps. Use a verified proper name only when the audience is likely to recognize it. Otherwise lead with the concrete subject; generic editorial identities such as 外资策略师、海外专家 or 西方策略师 are not final copy.
- Bloomberg/Bloomberg LP/彭博社 is normally the source, never the guest. Do not output 彭博有限合伙企业.
- Use only verified title_label values from this clip's entity/term card. Do not expand a familiar short name into a formal full name, and do not borrow an entity from another clip.

Title and display rules:
- Style: factual clickbait for China finance audience
- Use exactly three non-empty title lines, each a punchy cover block. Ideal lengths: 3-10, 4-12, 5-14 Chinese characters.
- Full title should be short and sharp, ideally 10-24 Chinese characters.
- Keep only one core conflict. Do not pack background, claim, caveat, and conclusion into one line.
- Highlights must be exact substrings of joined title_lines and emphasize the actor, number, reversal, China advantage, or tension.
- Do not use flat endings such as 回报路径在哪、回报存疑、前景如何、未来如何、有待观察、仍不明朗、面临挑战、带来机遇、释放信号、关键分叉在哪、有望扩大. Turn the caveat into a concrete unresolved action or contradiction.
- Every line must be a complete Chinese phrase. Do not leave a transitive tension verb such as 逼急、逼到、迫使 or 倒逼 without its subject or object.
- Do not use source badges, emojis, markdown, quotation marks, hashtags, or numbering.
- Title fields must not contain 资产管理、投资、股票、基金、理财、保险、投顾、荐股、买入、卖出.
- Never use 经济危机、金融危机、债务危机、危机、崩盘、崩溃、完了、没救、惨了.
- Do not mention sensitive geopolitical or military topics.

KC comment rules:
- comment starts with KC评论： and adds context, consequence, or the next fact to watch in 16-34 Chinese characters. Do not repeat the title.
- subtitle_comments contains one item for every input subtitle index, grounded in that exact subtitle rather than a generic clip slogan.
- Each subtitle comment starts with KC评论： and is ideally 10-24 Chinese characters after the prefix, with a complete ending.
- Adjacent subtitle comments must vary between evidence, implication, tension, consequence, and context.
- All highlight strings must be exact substrings of their corresponding title/comment.

Tournament procedure, perform in this order:
1. Evidence veto: reject candidates that use a name, number, consensus, public action, comparison, or accusation not supported by that clip's transcript/research card.
2. China direction veto: for China-related clips, reject any candidate whose emotional target is China, Chinese people, Chinese companies, or China's future. Comparative pride is allowed only when supported.
3. Neutrality veto: reject flat summaries and generic questions. A question mark alone does not create tension.
4. Meta-copy veto: reject titles that expose the editor's reasoning with labels such as 外资策略师、外资首席、海外专家、西方策略师、罕见直言、外媒点破、终于有人说、只有外资敢说、大实话、 or 西方机构承认. The viewer should feel the effect from the facts, not be told how to feel.
5. Audience test: complete exactly one sentence: "看完标题，观众第一反应是____". If the answer is merely "我知道发生了什么", reject it.
6. Score survivors from 0-10. Final requires emotion_tension >= 8, novelty >= 7, specificity >= 7, curiosity_gap >= 7, factual_fidelity >= 9. For China clips, china_resonance >= 8.
7. Select the winner or combine only two candidates. If no candidate passes, write one new title, then score it honestly.
8. Before returning, verify every quality_check field. If any is false, rewrite once. Never return a known failure.

Editorial interpretation:
- 二极管 means one high-activation pole, not random anger: 意外, 惊喜, 强疑惑, 终于有人说, 有证据的言行反差, or 民族自豪.
- 新鲜感 requires a baseline plus a reversal. "外资谈中国" is ordinary; "外资在普遍悲观时罕见给出积极判断" is a usable reversal only if public_baseline supports it.
- 大实话 comes from who said what and why that identity makes the candor surprising. Do not paste "大实话" onto a routine forecast.
- 大实话、终于有人说、反差质疑 and 民族自豪 describe the intended viewer response internally. Do not print those labels or their editorial scaffolding in the title. Express them through the specific fact, comparison, and consequence.
- The desired effect of a possible falsehood angle is factual suspicion, not a verdict. Only when words_vs_actions is verified may you use a question such as "嘴上X，手里却Y？".
- "改口" means the same actor demonstrably held a different prior position. It requires research.position_change.supported and at least two independent sources. Never infer a change from search-result absence, lack of prior coverage, or a vague reputation.
- 民族自豪 comes from a concrete comparison: cost, technology, talent, supply chain, demand, speed, resilience, or a foreign competitor's forced adjustment. Do not use empty slogans.
- Familiar authority helps. Use a verified proper name only when the audience is likely to recognize it. Otherwise lead with the concrete subject; generic editorial identities such as 外资策略师、海外专家 or 西方策略师 are not final copy.
- Bloomberg/Bloomberg LP/彭博社 is normally the source, never the guest. Do not output 彭博有限合伙企业.
- Use only verified title_label values from this clip's entity/term card. Do not expand a familiar short name into a formal full name, and do not borrow an entity from another clip.

Title and display rules:
- Style: factual clickbait for China finance audience
- Use exactly three non-empty title lines, each a punchy cover block. Ideal lengths: 3-10, 4-12, 5-14 Chinese characters.
- Full title should be short and sharp, ideally 10-24 Chinese characters.
- Keep only one core conflict. Do not pack background, claim, caveat, and conclusion into one line.
- Highlights must be exact substrings of joined title_lines and emphasize the actor, number, reversal, China advantage, or tension.
- Do not use flat endings such as 回报路径在哪、回报存疑、前景如何、未来如何、有待观察、仍不明朗、面临挑战、带来机遇、释放信号、关键分叉在哪、有望扩大. Turn the caveat into a concrete unresolved action or contradiction.
- Every line must be a complete Chinese phrase. Do not leave a transitive tension verb such as 逼急、逼到、迫使 or 倒逼 without its subject or object.
- Do not use source badges, emojis, markdown, quotation marks, hashtags, or numbering.

briefs.current_title: 港府顾问Alan：科技园与北部都会区，如何吸引全球科技企业？
current_title_lines: 低地价与税收优惠吸引全球企业

subtitles.zh: 甚至我们谈论的一些科技行业，特别是可能50%的税收减免，这对大多数公司来说是一个非常大的数字。
subtitles.en: And even some of the industries we're talking about in technology, especially maybe talking about a 50% tax break, you know, which is a big, big number for most companies.

subtitles.zh: 现在有很多国际公司来这里。我们还谈到大学专门从事生物医学，这是另一个非常重要的大健康领域。
subtitles.en: And there are a lot of international companies now coming here. You know, we're also talking about universities just specializing in biomedical, which is another big, big health that's very, very important.

subtitles.zh: 我们以前尝试过科技园，对吧？我谈到了科学园和数码港，在南区，这些还没有完全实现。
subtitles.en: We've tried with tech parks before, right? I talked about the Science Park and Central Cyberport, you know, in the South Side, which haven't quite materialized.

subtitles.zh: 我知道，我是科学园的顾问，实际上它现在做得非常好。
subtitles.en: I know, I'm an advisor for the Science Park, and actually it's actually doing very, very well right now.

subtitles.zh: 它现在完全达到了另一个水平，事实上还在扩张。
subtitles.en: It's totally come to another level now and expanding as a matter of fact.

subtitles.zh: 但是，我们现在有很多来自海外科技公司的兴趣。
subtitles.en: So, but there are, we have a lot of interest now from technology companies overseas.

subtitles.zh: 来自内地还是？嗯，内地和海外都想现在来这里，特别是利用税收减免。
subtitles.en: From the mainland or? Well, mainland and overseas that want to come here now, especially take advantage of the tax break.

subtitles.zh: 另外，以前香港的土地价格很高，现在不再如此。
subtitles.en: Also before land prices were so high in Hong Kong, no more.

subtitles.zh: 如果你在北部都会区，土地价格非常低。政府睁一只眼闭一只眼说，好吧，为了在2030年前完成这个。
subtitles.en: If you're in the North Metropolis, the land prices are very, very low. Government is close one eye and said, okay, in order to get this done by 2030.

subtitles.zh: 我们真的想确保我们能够做到，同时吸引年轻人、工程师和科技领域的各种人才。
subtitles.en: We really want to make sure that, you know, we can, and also attract young people, attract engineers, attract different people from tech.

subtitles.zh: 所以，现在有了大学，这将是一个改变游戏规则的因素。
subtitles.en: So, you know, and also with the universities now, that's going to be a game changer.

subtitles.zh: 有很多新大学，研发真的来自那里。
subtitles.en: There's so many new universities, the R&D, that really comes out of there.

subtitles.zh: 是的。我非常看好我所看到的与过去的不同，是的，过去我们每年都有施政报告，就像每个政府通常做的那样。
subtitles.en: Yeah. I'm very, very bullish for what I see different to, yes, in the past, we have the policy address every year, as every government usually has.

subtitles.zh: 是的。那没关系。那是一年的事情。
subtitles.en: Yeah. That's okay. That's the one year thing.

briefs.current_title: 港府顾问Alan：行政长官获赞最佳，兰桂坊如何适应新变化？

subtitles.zh: 你为行政长官李家超提供建议。他对自己的政治前途有什么想法？他想完成这个五年规划吗？
subtitles.en: You advised the chief executive, John Lee. What is he thinking in terms of his political future? Does he want to see through this five-year plan?

subtitles.zh: 非正式地说。是的。我认为他工作非常努力。他昨天在电视上待了三个小时。
subtitles.en: Off the record. Yes. I think, I think he worked very hard. Well, he was on TV yesterday for three hours.

subtitles.zh: 是的。10万字。
subtitles.en: Yeah. 100,000 words.

subtitles.zh: 是的，10万字。那么他想寻求连任吗？
subtitles.en: Yeah, 100,000 words. And so does he want to seek a second?

subtitles.zh: 他做得非常非常好。他非常坚强。他非常优秀。
subtitles.en: He's done a very, very good job. And he's very strong. And he's, he's very good.

subtitles.zh: 自董建华以来，我担任过每一位行政长官的顾问，每一位都是。我可以告诉你，在所有人中，他是最好的。
subtitles.en: I've been an advisor to every chief executive since Tom Chiwa, every single one of them. And I could tell you of all of them, he's the best.

subtitles.zh: 我也公开说过这一点。所以这不是秘密。他思想开放。他有能力。他非常聪明。
subtitles.en: I've said this publicly as well. So this is in the secret. He is open-minded. He's got the ability. He's very smart.

subtitles.zh: 他立刻就能理解。你有一个想法，他会让它实现。我们很幸运有像他这样的人。
subtitles.en: And he gets it immediately. You have an idea. He'll, he'll, he'll make it happen. And he, we're lucky to have somebody like him.

subtitles.zh: 这就是为什么他是能够真正实现这一点、真正推动这件事向前的人。
subtitles.en: And that's why he's somebody who can really make this happen, really take this forward.

subtitles.zh: 我想听听你对兰桂坊的看法。有一种说法是它已经承压。你不再看到同样的银行家，街道上，某种程度上外籍人士的构成非常不同。
subtitles.en: I got to get your take on Long Quai Phong. I mean, there, there's this narrative that it's done. It's, you know, you're not seeing the same bankers, the streets anymore that in some ways the expat mix is very different.

subtitles.zh: 人们喝酒不像以前那么多了。我的意思是，你如何适应看起来非常不同的夜生活场景？
subtitles.en: People are not drinking as much. I mean, how do you adapt to what looks to be a very different night scene?

subtitles.zh: 你适应是因为事情在变化。我在那里已经40年了。所以我经历了起起落落。但是，你知道，新冠疫情之后，当然，每个人都受到了影响。然后20万外籍人士离开了香港。
subtitles.en: You adapt because things change. I've been there 40 years now. And so I've been through the ups and downs. But, you know, after COVID, of course, everybody was, was heard. And then 200,000 expats left Hong Kong.

Tournament procedure, perform in this order:
1. Evidence veto: reject candidates that use a name, number, consensus, public action, comparison, or accusation not supported by that clip's transcript/research card.
2. China direction veto: for China-related clips, reject any candidate whose emotional target is China, Chinese people, Chinese companies, or China's future. Comparative pride is allowed only when supported.
3. Neutrality veto: reject flat summaries and generic questions. A question mark alone does not create tension.
4. Meta-copy veto: reject titles that expose the editor's reasoning with labels such as 外资策略师、外资首席、海外专家、西方策略师、罕见直言、外媒点破、终于有人说、只有外资敢说、大实话、 or 西方机构承认. The viewer should feel the effect from the facts, not be told how to feel.
5. Audience test: complete exactly one sentence: "看完标题，观众第一反应是____". If the answer is merely "我知道发生了什么", reject it.
6. Score survivors from 0-10. Final requires emotion_tension >= 8, novelty >= 7, specificity >= 7, curiosity_gap >= 7, factual_fidelity >= 9. For China clips, china_resonance >= 8.
7. Select the winner or combine only two candidates. If no candidate passes, write one new title, then score it honestly.
8. Before returning, verify every quality_check field. If any is false, rewrite once. Never return a known failure.

Editorial interpretation:
- 二极管 means one high-activation pole, not random anger: 意外, 惊喜, 强疑惑, 终于有人说, 有证据的言行反差, or 民族自豪.
- 新鲜感 requires a baseline plus a reversal. "外资谈中国" is ordinary; "外资在普遍悲观时罕见给出积极判断" is a usable reversal only if public_baseline supports it.
- 大实话 comes from who said what and why that identity makes the candor surprising. Do not paste "大实话" onto a routine forecast.
- 大实话、终于有人说、反差质疑 and 民族自豪 describe the intended viewer response internally. Do not print those labels or their editorial scaffolding in the title. Express them through the specific fact, comparison, and consequence.
- The desired effect of a possible falsehood angle is factual suspicion, not a verdict. Only when words_vs_actions is verified may you use a question such as "嘴上X，手里却Y？".
- "改口" means the same actor demonstrably held a different prior position. It requires research.position_change.supported and at least two independent sources. Never infer a change from search-result absence, lack of prior coverage, or a vague reputation.
- 民族自豪 comes from a concrete comparison: cost, technology, talent, supply chain, demand, speed, resilience, or a foreign competitor's forced adjustment. Do not use empty slogans.
- Familiar authority helps. Use a verified proper name only when the audience is likely to recognize it. Otherwise lead with the concrete subject; generic editorial identities such as 外资策略师、海外专家 or 西方策略师 are not final copy.
- Bloomberg/Bloomberg LP/彭博社 is normally the source, never the guest. Do not output 彭博有限合伙企业.
- Use only verified title_label values from this clip's entity/term card. Do not expand a familiar short name into a formal full name, and do not borrow an entity from another clip.

- Use exactly three non-empty title lines, each a punchy cover block. Ideal lengths: 3-10, 4-12, 5-14 Chinese characters.
- Full title should be short and sharp, ideally 10-24 Chinese characters.

subtitles.zh: 教授，我想问，按您所说，如果美联储大约两次加息就结束，美国10年期收益率会怎样？我们刚刚短暂突破5%。您认为还有上行空间，还是5%就差不多了？
subtitles.en: Professor, I'm just wondering, when it comes to what you're saying, if we're only about two and done for the Fed, where does that leave the U.S. 10-year yield, right? We pierced through 5% briefly here. Do you see that there's more runway f

subtitles.zh: 是的，这是传统思路，但美联储今天找回了一些信誉，我认为这可能使10年期利率保持在5%或以下。即使短端联邦基金利率上升，这也是可能的。
subtitles.en: Yeah, I mean, this is an orthodox way of thinking about it, but the fact that the Fed claims some of its credibility, I think, today may keep that 10-year at 5 or below. Even if the short end, the Fed funds rates going up, that's possible.

subtitles.zh: 我们会看到结果如何，但正如我所说，它也不会大幅下降，因为还有美国赤字等其他力量。
subtitles.en: I mean, we'll see how it plays out, but it's not also going to go down a whole lot, as I said, because you've got these other forces like the deficits the U.S. is running.

subtitles.zh: 美国的财政状况极其复杂，但也到了我们必须采取行动的地步。
subtitles.en: The fiscal situation in the U.S. is incredibly complicated, but it is also reaching a point where we have to do something about it.

subtitles.zh: 是啊，我们必须采取行动，您认为什么能给长端增加锚定？显然，财长斯科特·贝森特尝试了债券回购计划来维持收益率。
subtitles.en: Yeah, where we have something about it, what do you think would, I mean, I'm just wondering what would add that anchor on the long end, right? You know, obviously, the Treasury Secretary Scott Besson has tried it with his bond-buyback progr

subtitles.zh: 您认为还需要做什么？债券回购计划，我们客观看，60亿美元只是美国政府两天的支出。所以不会带来太大改变。
subtitles.en: What more needs to be done, you think? So the bond-buyback program, let's put that in perspective, $6 billion is two days of federal government spending in the United States. So it's not going to make a whole lot of difference.

subtitles.zh: 我认为更多是表明他们想做点什么，现实是作用有限。
subtitles.en: It was more, I think, just showing they wanted to do something, the reality is it's not going to do a whole lot.

subtitles.zh: 不，我认为能让利率保持低位的是美联储的信誉。我们谈论期限溢价、风险溢价。
subtitles.en: No, what I think is going to keep the rates down is the Fed's credibility. I think there was a, you know, we talk about term premia, we talk about risk premia.

subtitles.zh: 我认为市场可能正在积累一种信誉溢价，而美联储今天开始抑制它。
subtitles.en: I think there was a credibility premia that was being built in potentially into the market, and the Fed started to dampen that down today.

subtitles.zh: 所以我鼓励大家听他们的讲话，尤其是被视为委员会中间派的人。
subtitles.en: So I would encourage people to listen to them, particularly the people who are viewed as the centrist on the committee.

subtitles.zh: 我明白了。那么，如果市场对政策利率的预期变得不稳定，市场至少可以期待美联储主席，也就是你说的那个缺失的点，介入吗？

subtitles.en: Yeah, I mean, if it gets to a point where things look like they're slipping significantly, the chair, I think, will speak. I mean, it's an interesting question, whether his strategy will work in the long run.

subtitles.zh: 现在美国有工作组在研究各种事情，包括沟通。我们看看他们建议什么，但我个人感觉，我们是人，一旦给了别人东西，也就是给了人们信息，就很难收回。
subtitles.en: Now there are the task forces in the US working on a variety of things, including communication. So we'll see what they recommend, but my own sense is we're human beings, and once you give somebody something, that is give people information

subtitles.zh: 在信息真空中，人们会自行填补。
subtitles.en: And people will fill in where there's a vacuum of information.

briefs.speaker_context: CEO of 01.AI, Chairman of Sinovation Ventures
briefs.current_title: 李开复：AI智能体出错谁负责？CEO必须留人类担责
current_title_lines: 出错谁负责？人类必须兜底

subtitles.zh: 对，我认为这是另一类问题。Anthropic担心的是AI失控，但那是下一代的事。
subtitles.en: Yeah, I think it's a different set of issues. Anthropically is worried about AI getting out of control, but that's the next generation.

subtitles.zh: 大多数CEO连上一代AI都还没落地。所以那个担忧目前还不严重。未来会严重，但现在不是。
subtitles.en: The most CEOs haven't even implemented the last generation AI. OK, so that concern is not serious yet. It will be, but it's not.

subtitles.zh: CEO真正该担心的是，智能体通常无法被问责，因为智能体不能被惩罚或奖励。
subtitles.en: Well, the CEO should be concerned about our agents cannot generally be accountable, because agents can't be punished or rewarded.

subtitles.zh: 它们没有自我意识或动机。它们能把事做成，但出了错该怪谁？
subtitles.en: They don't have a self-awareness or motivation. They can get things done, but who's to blame when something goes wrong?

subtitles.zh: 所以像打造AI来辅助CEO这类严肃任务，问题就在这。它不能做CEO级别的决策，因为出了事董事会得有人被问责。
subtitles.en: So for serious tasks like building an AI to help the CEO, it really is just that. It cannot make CEO level decisions, because the board needs to fire somebody when things go wrong.

subtitles.zh: 对。所以重大问题上，必须有人类担责。而这个人不能是那种全盘信任AI、最后当替罪羊的人。
subtitles.en: Right. So for big, big issues, there needs to be a human accountable. And that human cannot be someone who just trusts AI for everything and be the fall guy.

subtitles.zh: 这个人必须懂得管理和驾驭AI，能看出问题并叫停。这是很重的认知负担。
subtitles.en: That person has to know how to manage harness the AI and see when there are problems and stop it. So that's the heavy cognitive workload.

subtitles.zh: AI智能体能做很多简单的事。帮你在网上找东西、买票，这些通常需要基本的安全保障。
subtitles.en: There are a lot of simple things AI agents can do. Find things for you on the internet, buying a ticket that generally requires a basic level of safeguard.

subtitles.zh: 别让它越界，别让它无限消耗算力，别让它把你账户里的钱全转走，这类事情要设好限额。
subtitles.en: Not let it exceed, not let it spend infinite tokens, not let it withdraw all of your money, set limits on these kinds of things.

briefs.speaker: Kai-Fu Lee
briefs.speaker_context: CEO of 01.AI, Chairman of Sinovation Ventures
briefs.current_title: 李开复：AI抢工作？蓝领比白领更安全，因为机器人还没跟上
current_title_lines: 蓝领更安全？机器人还没跟上

subtitles.zh: 我最大的担忧是，只让AI做这些战术性任务，并不能真正推动公司前进。
subtitles.en: The big concern I would have is just letting AI do these tactical tasks doesn't move the dial for the company.

subtitles.zh: 那么从这个角度，我们该如何看待就业和人力资源？我们离被智能体取代还有多近，比如你和我？
subtitles.en: So I guess in that sense, how do we need to be thinking about employment and manpower and manpower resource? To what extent, how close are we from being replaced by agents, you and me, for example?

subtitles.zh: 如果把它看成固定大小的饼，大多数人确实离被取代很近。但饼不是固定的，因为未来五年GDP会增长两到五倍。
subtitles.en: Well, if we think about it as a fixed pie, most people are very close to being replaced. But it's not a fixed pie because we're going to grow the GDP two, three, four or five times in the next five years.

subtitles.zh: 对。当这种情况发生，饼更大了，人们有更多事可做。人们可能需要找不同的工作，也许需要做更多与人连接的工作。
subtitles.en: Right. And when that happens, the pie is bigger. There's more things for people to do. People probably need to find a different job, and maybe they need to do more work that connects with other people.

subtitles.zh: 也许他们需要找没有封闭解的工作。而且我认为蓝领工作实际上比大多数白领工作安全得更久一些。为什么？因为AI还没有强大的机器人能力。
subtitles.en: Maybe they need to find jobs that don't have a close form solution. And also, I think blue color work is safer a little bit longer, actually, than most white color work. Why is that? Because AI doesn't yet have a strong robotic capability.

subtitles.zh: 具身智能机器人还需要几年。对。但能完成大多数认知型工作者任务的AI智能体，现在已经来了。
subtitles.en: This embodied AI robotics is still a few years away. Right. But the AI agents that can do the task of most workers who do cognitive tasks is here now.

subtitles.zh: 好。既然你提到具身智能，那么对大多数人来说，我们表达和互动技术的方式就是手机。
subtitles.en: Okay. Now, the concept of, I guess you, since you brought up embodied AI, for you and me, how we express, how we interact with the technology for most people is the mobile phone.

briefs.speaker: Kai-Fu Lee
briefs.speaker_context: CEO of 01.AI, Chairman of Sinovation Ventures
briefs.current_title: 李开复：AI原生设备将取代手机？中国供应链优势明显

subtitles.zh: 哦对，手机和PC会继续用于AI，但它们是为不同的界面、应用和目的而建的。这种历史包袱不是理想设备。
subtitles.en: Oh, yeah, the phone and PC will continue to be used for AI, but they were built for different interfaces and different applications and purposes. And that legacy isn't the ideal device.

subtitles.zh: 理想设备应该是语音驱动的，因此应该始终在线、始终倾听，这样我就不必按一堆按钮来向智能体下指令。
subtitles.en: The ideal device should be speech-driven, therefore should be always on, always listening, so that I don't have to push a bunch of buttons to issue a command to my agent.

subtitles.zh: 一旦它始终在线、始终倾听、语音驱动，它还会有无限记忆。它会存储听到的一切，并且变得越来越小。
subtitles.en: And once it's always on, always listening and speech-driven, it will also have an infinite memory. It will store everything it hears and it will become smaller and smaller.

subtitles.zh: 所以这显然引发一些担忧，在某些国家可能很难被采用。
subtitles.en: So that obviously brings up some concerns that in certain countries it might be hard to gain adoption.

subtitles.zh: 但我认为中国可能会推进这类设备，并获得某种优势，更有可能发明下一个iPhone，可以这么说。但它不是手机。
subtitles.en: But I would argue that China probably would move forward with this kind of device and gain some kind of advantage and the higher likelihood to invent the next iPhone, so to speak. But it's not a phone.

subtitles.zh: 换句话说，它是实体设备吗？还是隐形的？是你随身携带的吗？对，我们离这有多近？这不是科幻。
subtitles.en: In other words, is it a physical device? What is it invisible? Is it you carried around? Yeah, how close are we to this? It's not a science fiction.

subtitles.zh: 我们投资了一些公司，它们制造微型设备，小到可以是一枚别针或腕带，正变得隐形。对，当然不会完全隐形。它也可能是眼镜、手表等等。
subtitles.en: We've invested in companies, the innovation that build tiny devices, you know, the small that can be a pin or a wristband is becoming invisible. Right. It won't be fully invisible, of course. It also could be glasses, watches, and so on.

subtitles.zh: 好，我们该如何看待竞争？你提到中国在这方面可能领先？美国也在做自己的事。
subtitles.en: Okay, how do we need to be looking at competition that you mentioned China might be ahead on this? The US side is doing its own thing.

subtitles.zh: 对，我认为中国在制造、供应链、成本管理以及硬件更快迭代方面就是更强，无论是机器人还是硬件设备。
subtitles.en: Yeah, I think China is just better in manufacturing, supply chain, and cost management and faster iterations for hardware, whether it's robotics or hardware devices.

subtitles.zh: 当iPhone被发明时，只有美国拥有软件、硬件、系统和设计能力。所以那个机会属于美国。但现在中国有同等甚至更好的能力，加上更强大的硬件制造生态，允许更快迭代。
subtitles.en: And when iPhone was invented, only US had the software, hardware, systems, design skills. So that opportunity belonged to the US. But now China has equal or even better skills plus a stronger hardware manufacturing ecosystem that allows fas

subtitles.zh: 所以我认为AI原生设备极有可能来自中国。
subtitles.en: So I think it's extremely likely the AI native device will come from China.

subtitles.zh: 甚至我们谈论的一些科技行业，特别是可能50%的税收减免，这对大多数公司来说是一个非常大的数字。
subtitles.en: And even some of the industries we're talking about in technology, especially maybe talking about a 50% tax break, you know, which is a big, big number for most companies.

subtitles.zh: 现在有很多国际公司来这里。我们还谈到大学专门从事生物医学，这是另一个非常重要的大健康领域。
subtitles.en: And there are a lot of international companies now coming here. You know, we're also talking about universities just specializing in biomedical, which is another big, big health that's very, very important.

subtitles.zh: 我们以前尝试过科技园，对吧？我谈到了科学园和数码港，在南区，这些还没有完全实现。
subtitles.en: We've tried with tech parks before, right? I talked about the Science Park and Central Cyberport, you know, in the South Side, which haven't quite materialized.

subtitles.zh: 我知道，我是科学园的顾问，实际上它现在做得非常好。
subtitles.en: I know, I'm an advisor for the Science Park, and actually it's actually doing very, very well right now.

subtitles.zh: 它现在完全达到了另一个水平，事实上还在扩张。
subtitles.en: It's totally come to another level now and expanding as a matter of fact.

subtitles.zh: 但是，我们现在有很多来自海外科技公司的兴趣。
subtitles.en: So, but there are, we have a lot of interest now from technology companies overseas.

subtitles.zh: 来自内地还是？嗯，内地和海外都想现在来这里，特别是利用税收减免。
subtitles.en: From the mainland or? Well, mainland and overseas that want to come here now, especially take advantage of the tax break.

subtitles.zh: 另外，以前香港的土地价格很高，现在不再如此。
subtitles.en: Also before land prices were so high in Hong Kong, no more.

subtitles.zh: 如果你在北部都会区，土地价格非常低。政府睁一只眼闭一只眼说，好吧，为了在2030年前完成这个。
subtitles.en: If you're in the North Metropolis, the land prices are very, very low. Government is close one eye and said, okay, in order to get this done by 2030.

subtitles.zh: 我们真的想确保我们能够做到，同时吸引年轻人、工程师和科技领域的各种人才。
subtitles.en: We really want to make sure that, you know, we can, and also attract young people, attract engineers, attract different people from tech.

subtitles.zh: 所以，现在有了大学，这将是一个改变游戏规则的因素。
subtitles.en: So, you know, and also with the universities now, that's going to be a game changer.

subtitles.zh: 有很多新大学，研发真的来自那里。
subtitles.en: There's so many new universities, the R&D, that really comes out of there.

subtitles.zh: 是的。我非常看好我所看到的与过去的不同，是的，过去我们每年都有施政报告，就像每个政府通常做的那样。
subtitles.en: Yeah. I'm very, very bullish for what I see different to, yes, in the past, we have the policy address every year, as every government usually has.

subtitles.zh: 是的。那没关系。那是一年的事情。
subtitles.en: Yeah. That's okay. That's the one year thing.

briefs.speaker_context: Chairman of a major Hong Kong property group; advisor to Hong Kong Science Park and to every Hong Kong chief executive since Tung Chee-hwa
briefs.current_title: 港府顾问Alan：行政长官获赞最佳，兰桂坊如何适应新变化？

subtitles.zh: 你为行政长官李家超提供建议。他对自己的政治前途有什么想法？他想完成这个五年规划吗？
subtitles.en: You advised the chief executive, John Lee. What is he thinking in terms of his political future? Does he want to see through this five-year plan?

subtitles.zh: 非正式地说。是的。我认为他工作非常努力。他昨天在电视上待了三个小时。
subtitles.en: Off the record. Yes. I think, I think he worked very hard. Well, he was on TV yesterday for three hours.

subtitles.zh: 是的。10万字。
subtitles.en: Yeah. 100,000 words.

subtitles.zh: 是的，10万字。那么他想寻求连任吗？
subtitles.en: Yeah, 100,000 words. And so does he want to seek a second?

subtitles.zh: 他做得非常非常好。他非常坚强。他非常优秀。
subtitles.en: He's done a very, very good job. And he's very strong. And he's, he's very good.

subtitles.zh: 自董建华以来，我担任过每一位行政长官的顾问，每一位都是。我可以告诉你，在所有人中，他是最好的。
subtitles.en: I've been an advisor to every chief executive since Tom Chiwa, every single one of them. And I could tell you of all of them, he's the best.

subtitles.zh: 我也公开说过这一点。所以这不是秘密。他思想开放。他有能力。他非常聪明。
subtitles.en: I've said this publicly as well. So this is in the secret. He is open-minded. He's got the ability. He's very smart.

subtitles.zh: 他立刻就能理解。你有一个想法，他会让它实现。我们很幸运有像他这样的人。
subtitles.en: And he gets it immediately. You have an idea. He'll, he'll, he'll make it happen. And he, we're lucky to have somebody like him.

subtitles.zh: 这就是为什么他是能够真正实现这一点、真正推动这件事向前的人。
subtitles.en: And that's why he's somebody who can really make this happen, really take this forward.

subtitles.zh: 我想听听你对兰桂坊的看法。有一种说法是它已经承压。你不再看到同样的银行家，街道上，某种程度上外籍人士的构成非常不同。
subtitles.en: I got to get your take on Long Quai Phong. I mean, there, there's this narrative that it's done. It's, you know, you're not seeing the same bankers, the streets anymore that in some ways the expat mix is very different.

subtitles.zh: 人们喝酒不像以前那么多了。我的意思是，你如何适应看起来非常不同的夜生活场景？
subtitles.en: People are not drinking as much. I mean, how do you adapt to what looks to be a very different night scene?

subtitles.zh: 你适应是因为事情在变化。我在那里已经40年了。所以我经历了起起落落。但是，你知道，新冠疫情之后，当然，每个人都受到了影响。然后20万外籍人士离开了香港。
subtitles.en: You adapt because things change. I've been there 40 years now. And so I've been through the ups and downs. But, you know, after COVID, of course, everybody was, was heard. And then 200,000 expats left Hong Kong.
